subject.title: Feature request: native Codex quota/auth diagnosis plus brokered reauth execution

question: What native OpenAI/Codex recovery-state contract and broker trust boundary should OpenClaw support for quota waits versus reauth-required failures?
rationale: The remaining work is not a narrow bug fix: it changes provider auth semantics, Gateway/UI contracts, channel recovery behavior, and potentially host-side OAuth execution authority.

options.title: Contract first, broker later
options.body: Define `quota_wait` and `reauth_required` as typed provider/Gateway/UI states now, then add any broker behind explicit operator authorization and audit requirements.

options.title: Plugin-owned broker
options.body: Keep core limited to diagnosis and expose only the minimal plugin/host API needed for an external broker to implement reauth safely.

options.title: Full native broker
options.body: Build a first-party brokered reauth path in core, accepting the larger security review and upgrade surface.

recommendation.title: Contract first, broker later
recommendation.body: Define `quota_wait` and `reauth_required` as typed provider/Gateway/UI states now, then add any broker behind explicit operator authorization and audit requirements.

likelyOwner.reason: They have the strongest recent history across the Gateway auth-status, Codex quota, and auth recovery surfaces that this decision spans.
